label: override_express
point: Held that mitigating measures must be considered in deciding whether an impairment substantially limits a major life activity, relying on the ADA findings (including the 43 million figure) to read 'disability' narrowly.
change: The ADAAA rewrote the 12101 findings (dropping the 43 million and 'discrete and insular minority' findings) and redefined disability to exclude consideration of mitigating measures.
why: The Act's findings name Sutton as having narrowed the ADA's intended scope and the amendments reverse its mitigating-measures rule and the findings it relied on.

label: unrelated
point: Described the Colorado River Storage Project Act (43 U.S.C. 620) as background authority for the San Juan-Chama Project in interpreting Reclamation contracts and ESA duties.
change: Added the Navajo-Gallup Water Supply Project to the list of participating projects in 620.
why: Adding a participating project has nothing to do with the decision's contract/ESA point; the law mentions the litigation only in a savings clause.

label: related
point: Applied the Sentencing Guidelines (2B5.3, 2X1.1) to value counterfeit packaging for a 2320(a) conviction, requiring a reasonable-certainty finding and a 3-level attempt reduction.
change: Extended 2320(a) to trafficking in counterfeit labels, packaging and similar items, and separately directed the Sentencing Commission to consider such cases, citing Sung.
why: The amendment to 2320(a) widens the offence but does not change the Guidelines rules the court applied; the case is named only in a directive to the Sentencing Commission to take it into account.

label: override_express
point: Held that a Title VII pay-discrimination charge is untimely unless filed within 180 days of the discriminatory pay decision, not of later paychecks.
change: Added 2000e-5(e)(3) making each paycheck affected by a discriminatory compensation decision a new unlawful employment practice that restarts the charge period.
why: The Act names Ledbetter in its findings and directly reverses its timeliness rule.

label: override_implicit
point: Held that FCLAA 1334(b) pre-empts Massachusetts' location-based restrictions on outdoor and point-of-sale cigarette advertising.
change: Amended 1334(a) to let FDA require different package warnings, and the same Act added 1334(c) letting States impose time, place and manner (not content) restrictions on cigarette advertising.
why: The new 1334(c) removes pre-emption for exactly the location restrictions Lorillard held pre-empted; the law names Lorillard only for First Amendment guidance on FDA rules, not as the reason for the pre-emption change.

label: override_express
point: Held the CPPA's 'appears to be' a minor (2256(8)(B)) and 'conveys the impression' (2256(8)(D)) definitions overbroad under the First Amendment.
change: The PROTECT Act rewrote 2256(8) (computer-generated images 'indistinguishable from' real minors), replaced (D) with a pandering offence, and raised 2251 penalties.
why: The Act's findings and report identify Free Speech Coalition and the law rewrites the very definitions it struck down; the 2251 changes themselves are penalties.

label: unrelated
point: Exercised Federal Circuit jurisdiction under 1295(a)(3) over a Court of Federal Claims tax-depletion appeal.
change: Renamed PTO officials in 1295(a)(4) and added 154(b) appeals.
why: Changes concern patent-office appeals, not Claims Court jurisdiction; the Exxon named is the Exxon Valdez consent decree, a different case.

label: related
point: Treated Williams as substantially limited in performing manual tasks by reference to her work tasks, under the ADA generally (42 U.S.C. 12101 et seq.).
change: The ADAAA rewrote the 12101 findings and purposes, rejecting the Supreme Court's Toyota v. Williams standard that reversed this decision.
why: Congress rejected the Supreme Court decision that reversed this one, so the change does not undercut this decision's result; the cited findings were only a citation to the Act.

label: codifies
point: Assessed Georgia's revised Senate plan under the Section 5 retrogression test, focusing on minority voters' ability to elect candidates of choice.
change: Added 1973c(b)-(d) defining prohibited effect as diminishing citizens' ability to elect their preferred candidates of choice and covering any discriminatory purpose.
why: The 2006 Act rejects the Supreme Court's Georgia v. Ashcroft totality test and restores the ability-to-elect standard the district court applied, so it agrees with this court's approach.

label: related
point: Held that ANILCA 'public lands' for the subsistence priority include navigable waters in which the United States holds reserved water rights.
change: Added definitions of customary and traditional uses, customary trade and rural Alaska resident to 3113 (with related changes to 3114-3115).
why: The new definitions concern the scope of subsistence uses, not which waters are public lands; McDowell, named in the law, is a different case.

label: codifies
point: On remand, vacated restitution orders so that 2259 restitution is set by the defendant's relative role in the causal process, per the Supreme Court's Paroline decision.
change: Added 2259(b)(2) setting trafficking restitution at an amount reflecting the defendant's relative role in the causal process, with a $3,000 floor and a cap at full losses.
why: The law writes the Paroline relative-role standard into 2259 and cites the Supreme Court decision approvingly, adding a minimum.

label: override_express
point: Held that 18 U.S.C. 116(a) (FGM) exceeded Congress's Commerce Clause and Necessary and Proper powers.
change: Rewrote 116 to add interstate/foreign commerce and other jurisdictional elements and broaden the offence.
why: Congress states the court erred in Nagarwala and rewrote the section so its Commerce Clause reasoning no longer applies.

label: related
point: Granted certiorari on what causal nexus is required for restitution under 2259, deciding nothing on the merits.
change: Added 2259(b)(2) setting restitution by the defendant's relative role in the causal process, with a $3,000 floor.
why: The law addresses the question certified, but the order held nothing the law could reverse or codify; it cites the later merits decision in the same case.

label: unrelated
point: Cited 15 U.S.C. 1333 as an example of tobacco-specific legislation in denying a separation-of-powers summary judgment motion against the RICO claims.
change: Replaced the Surgeon General's warnings in 1333 with new graphic warning requirements.
why: The new warnings have nothing to do with whether tobacco legislation bars RICO claims; the Act cites a 2006 ruling in the same litigation only for its factual findings.

label: codifies
point: Held that 'analogue' of fentanyl in 841(b)(1)(B)(vi) takes its ordinary meaning, so a scheduled substance like butyryl fentanyl qualifies.
change: Added 'or a fentanyl-related substance' to the fentanyl analogue penalty clauses of 841(b)(1)(A)(vi) and (B)(vi).
why: The Act expressly states Congress agrees with the district court's interpretation in McCray, which this decision affirmed, and extends the penalties consistently.
